title: Malagasy lamba silk weaving
summary: The lamba is the wrapped cloth of Madagascar, and its finest silk form is woven on a low ground loom in long coloured warp stripes, with extra weft threads floated across to make bands of diamonds and zigzags. Highland weavers shaped the style, and a small group of workshops keeps it alive.
howToPlay: Choose a silk colour and a motif from the strip under the cloth.
Tap a square to weave it: the left half of the cloth is copied to the right, as the two selvedges of a lamba mirror each other.
Match the small design shown above the cloth, then press Check.
rules: The cloth is a mirror across its centre line: whatever you weave on one side appears on the other.
A square counts only when its motif and its silk colour both match the design.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you may undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Silk and cotton lambas have been woven in the highlands of Madagascar by Merina and Betsileo weavers, and the richly patterned silk cloth was revived in workshops in the 1990s after the skill had nearly been lost.
